summary: Senedd Research published an article on 24 September 2026 finding that summer 2026 was the hottest on record in Wales by average June to August temperature, almost 3C above the late twentieth century average, after the hottest spring and a driest, joint-hottest July. Wales had its first red extreme heat warning, official heatwaves in every month from May to August and marine heatwave conditions in Welsh seas for most of the summer. Fire and rescue services declared four major wildfire incidents in July and August, and the First Minister said he would convene a climate change and resilience summit on wildfires in October 2026.
title: Summer 2026 was the hottest on record in Wales, with the first red extreme heat warning and persistent marine heatwave conditions
